clue.text: Animal's means of control — costly by the sound of it

parts.note: a rein is the strap used to control a horse

indicators.note: says the word for costly is to be heard, not spelt, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: costly means dear

explanation.surface: A rider's reins, and an expensive horse's upkeep, seem to be the topic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('Animal is ...'). DEAR spoken gives DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer is an Arctic animal of the deer family.

clue.text: Income still invested in French way

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rue is the French word for a street
still, as in 'still more', means even

explanation.surface: Money is still being put into a French street project.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is a synonym for income, especially that of a state or business.

clue.text: Put in vessel, I race up north

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for race is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to race is to run

explanation.surface: Someone loads things into a ship before rushing northward.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place ashes in an urn, a funerary vessel.

clue.text: Recklessly altered, mint can become harmful

indicators.note: done recklessly, the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Carelessly tampering with a mint, or its coins, can cause damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Detrimental is a synonym for harmful or damaging.

clue.text: Pass English Liberal going over part of church

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over places the first pieces above the next

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: An English Liberal politician walks past a church's far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: First-class article about Mahler's last song

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the composer's name

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A top-rate essay concerning the final song in a Mahler cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song, as in opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Composer and Antarctic explorer in one

parts.note: Sir James Clark Ross explored the Antarctic, giving his name to the Ross Sea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One person is said to be both a composer and a polar explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: King visiting Irish islands, or a Scottish one

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the king's letter goes inside

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch tours Ireland's islands, or perhaps one in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde in Scotland; 'one' stands for an island.

clue.text: Show off verse written by relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A poem composed by a family member is flaunted.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaunt is to boast about or parade something proudly.

clue.text: Indicter, a person who employs about two hundred

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces wrap the numeral

parts.note: one who employs, i.e. uses, something is a user
CC is two hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An accuser is described as an employer of some two hundred staff.
explanation.definitionFit: One who indicts formally charges someone, which is what an accuser does.

clue.text: Grain: formerly old Tyneside mainstay

parts.note: corn is grain
erst is an archaic word for formerly
Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Grain was once the old backbone of the Tyneside economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornerstone is the foundation or chief support of something, a mainstay.

clue.text: One who has taken vows? Not any, some say

indicators.note: some say means spoken aloud, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: not any means none

explanation.surface: People debate whether anyone has truly taken vows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun takes religious vows of poverty, chastity and obedience.

clue.text: Implant is not in centre of tree, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly arranged, so the letters are rearranged
centre of takes the middle letters of the word tree

explanation.surface: Remarkably, a graft has not been placed in the heart of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An implant is something inserted, so the noun insertion fits it.

clue.text: Returning, encounters Eastern regard

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for encounters is read backwards

parts.note: encounters, as a verb, means meets

explanation.surface: Someone coming back meets with respect in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard someone highly is to esteem them; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Much upset about mob breaking up lottery

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed phrase goes around the jumbled letters
upset, in a down clue, turns the phrase for much upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: much means a lot

indicators.note: breaking up means falling apart, so the letters of mob are jumbled

explanation.surface: Many are angry about a crowd disrupting a prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: ALOT read backwards is TOLA; MOB rearranged is MBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery in which tickets are drawn from a revolving drum, often at a fete.

clue.text: European residing in very pleasant Italian city

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A European lives in a delightful Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the Italian city of canals on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Divorcee given a pit to inspect

parts.note: a divorcee is an ex, a former spouse
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A divorced person is handed a coal pit to look over.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect closely; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Forge, initially, should mould iron to help you

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workshop is advised to shape iron to help you.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's workshop, where metal is forged.

clue.text: Quite a source of news and comment — now and then!

parts.note: some, as in 'that was some party', means quite a
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a newspaper's occasional brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometimes means occasionally, from time to time.

clue.text: Press employee takes hour in identifying woody plant

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the hour's letters are held
in confirms the hour's letters go inside the employee

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, works on a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper worker spends an hour naming a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, with several stems.

clue.text: Turkish commander going to and fro

definitions.note: an Ottoman officer or chief bore this title, also spelt agha

indicators.note: to and fro means the same either way, so the word reads identically in both directions

parts.note: an Ottoman officer or chief bore this title, also spelt agha

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer is pacing back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was an Ottoman military commander or official.

clue.text: District accommodating new stadium, perhaps

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the letter for new goes inside

parts.note: a district is an area

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood makes room for a new sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is one example of an arena, a venue for sport or spectacle.

clue.text: Marsupial allowed to eat top of this plant part

indicators.note: to eat means taking in, so the first pieces swallow a letter

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial
allowed means let

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word this

explanation.surface: A kangaroo is permitted to nibble the top of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootlet is a small root, a part of a plant.

clue.text: Daggers bishop plunged into old priest

indicators.note: plunged into means thrust inside, so the bishop's letter goes in

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop drives daggers into an elderly priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped printing marks, also called obelisks, used for footnotes.

clue.text: Old railway publicity that has its point?

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: Old British Rail advertising seems to make a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin nail with a small head, something with a sharp tip.

clue.text: The kind to confront design of print

parts.note: a type is a kind
to confront is to face

explanation.surface: A printer of that sort faces up to a design.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is the particular design of lettering used in printing.
